Surah Luqman [Meccan, except verses 27, 28 and 29, which are Medinan; its verses number 34; it was revealed after As-Saffat]

﴿Alif. Lam. Mim.﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 2:

﴿Tilka﴾ i.e., these: the verses ﴿of the Book﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿the Wise﴾, possessed of wisdom. The idafa (genitive construction) here carries the meaning of "from" (min), i.e., "the verses from the Book."

﴿Guidance and mercy﴾ [is read] in the nominative (raf'). In the reading of the majority, it is in the accusative (nasb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial qualifier) of "the verses" (al-āyāt). The element governing it is the sense of indication (ishāra) contained in "those" (﴿tilka﴾).

﴿Those who establish prayer﴾ is an explanation (*bayān*, explanatory clarification) of "the doers of good" (*al-muḥsinīn*), ﴿and give zakat, and they, in the Hereafter, are certain﴾. The second *hum* (هُمْ) is an emphatic restatement (*ta'kīd*, emphasis).
﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful﴾ (al-Mufliḥūn), meaning the victorious (al-Fā'izūn).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 6:

﴿And among people is one who purchases idle talk﴾, i.e., that which diverts from what is of benefit, ﴿to mislead﴾ (with the yāʾ read both with a fatḥa and with a ḍamma) ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, the path of Islam, ﴿without knowledge, and take it﴾ (with the verb in the accusative, as a conjunction with yuḍilla, and in the nominative, as a conjunction with yashtarī) ﴿in mockery﴾, being mocked at with it. ﴿Those will have a humiliating punishment﴾, one that brings humiliation.

The Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 31, verse 7:

﴿And when Our verses are recited to him,﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿he turns away arrogantly,﴾ i.e., proudly, ﴿as if he had not heard them, as if there were deafness in his ears.﴾ i.e., deafness. The two clauses of simile are circumstantial clauses (ḥāl) relating to the pronoun in "turns away," or the second is an explanation (bayān) of the first. ﴿So give him good tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ i.e., inform him ﴿of a painful punishment,﴾ i.e., one that causes pain. The mention of "good tidings" is mockery of him. He was al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who used to go to al-Ḥīra on trading trips, buy books of the stories of the non-Arabs (al-ʿAjam), and relate them to the people of Mecca, saying: "Muhammad tells you the stories of ʿĀd and Thamūd, and I will tell you the stories of Persia (Fārs) and the Byzantines (al-Rūm)." They would find his narration pleasing and would abandon listening to the Qur'an.

Abiding therein forever (khalidina fiha): a circumstantial clause (hal) taken as anticipated, meaning: their abiding in it is decreed for them when they enter it. ﴿The promise of Allah, truly.﴾ That is, Allah promised them this, and His promise is true, truly. ﴿And He is the Almighty﴾ who nothing overcomes so as to prevent Him from fulfilling His promise and His threat, ﴿the All-Wise﴾ who places nothing except in its proper place.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 10:

﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you can see.﴾ That is, the pillars (ʿumud) are the plural of ʿimad, which is a column; and the verse is true whether there are no pillars at all. ﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains﴾ high mountains ﴿lest﴾ it should not ﴿shake﴾ move ﴿with you. And He scattered in it creatures of every kind. And We sent down﴾ here there is an iltifat (shift) from the third person (ghaybah) ﴿from the sky water, and We caused to grow in it every noble pair﴾ every fine kind.

This is the Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 31, verse 11:

﴿This is the creation of Allah﴾, i.e., His creation. ﴿So show me﴾, i.e., inform me, O people of Makkah, ﴿what those besides Him have created﴾, other than Him, i.e., your gods, that you associate them with Him, exalted is He. The interrogative "mā" is for censure, and it is the subject (mubtada'), and "dhā" in the sense of "alladhī" with its relative clause is the predicate (khabar). "Arūnī" is suspended from governing (mu'allaq 'an al-'amal), and what follows it fills the place of the two objects. ﴿Rather﴾ (bal) is for transition. ﴿The wrongdoers are in manifest error﴾, clear, by their associating others with Him, and you are among them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 12:

﴿And We certainly gave Luqman wisdom﴾ — of it, knowledge, religious observance, and correctness in speech. His sayings are many and transmitted. He used to give legal rulings (yufti) before the mission of Dawud, and he lived to see his mission and took knowledge from him, and he gave up giving rulings. He said concerning that: "Shall I not be content when I have been sufficed?" It was said to him: "Which of people is the worst?" He said: "The one who does not care if people see him doing wrong."

﴿that﴾ — i.e., And We said to him, that ﴿give thanks to Allah﴾ for what He has given you of wisdom. ﴿And whoever gives thanks, he gives thanks only for himself﴾, because the reward of his thanks is for himself. ﴿And whoever is ungrateful﴾ for the favour, ﴿then indeed Allah is Free of need﴾ from His creation, ﴿Praiseworthy﴾, praised in His doing.

and (remember) when Luqman said to his son, while he was admonishing him: "O my little son" (a diminutive expressing affection), "do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association (shirk) with Allah is a great wrong," so he returned to him (in faith) and embraced Islam.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 14:

﴿And We enjoined upon man (concerning) his parents⌋ We commanded him to be good to them. ﴿His mother carried him﴾ and became weak, ﴿weakness upon weakness﴾, i.e., she became weak for the carrying, weak for the labour pains, and weak for the delivery. ﴿And his weaning﴾, i.e., his weaning (from milk), ﴿is in two years﴾. And We said to him: ﴿Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the (final) destination﴾, i.e., the return.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 15:

﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge﴾ [meaning: this is] in accordance with the reality (muwafaqa lil-waqi'). ﴿Then do not obey them, but keep them company in this world with kindness (ma'ruf)﴾ i.e., with what is known to be good: righteousness (al-birr) and maintaining ties (al-sila). ﴿And follow the way (sabil) of one who turns back (anab) [to Me]﴾ i.e., returns (raja'a) ﴿to Me﴾ in obedience. ﴿Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾ i.e., I will recompense you for it. The clause of the injunction and what follows it is a parenthetical interjection (i'tiraD).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 16:

﴿O my son, indeed it﴾ i.e., the wrong deed (al-khaslah al-sayyi'ah), ﴿if it should be the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or within the heavens or within the earth﴾ i.e., in the most hidden place of that, ﴿Allah will bring it forth.﴾ So He will call to account for it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle﴾ in extracting it, ﴿Acquainted﴾ with its place.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 17:

﴿O my son, establish the prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you﴾ because of the enjoining and forbidding. ﴿Indeed, that﴾ mentioned [matter] ﴿is among the matters requiring resolve﴾, i.e., among the things that are resolved upon (ma'zumat), which one resolves to do because they are obligatory.

﴿And do not turn your cheek﴾. A variant recitation (qira'ah) reads: تُصاعِر (tusa'ir). ﴿away from people﴾: do not turn your face away from them out of arrogance. ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly﴾, i.e., in conceit. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love every arrogant, boastful one﴾: one who struts in his walk, ﴿boasting over people﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 19:

﴿And be moderate in your walking﴾ — be midway in it between the slow plodding and the hasty rushing, and let upon you be tranquility and dignity. ﴿And lower your voice﴾ — lower it ﴿from your voice. Indeed, the most hateful of voices﴾ — the most ugly of them ﴿is the voice of donkeys﴾ — its beginning is an exhalation (zafir) and its end is an inhalation (shahiq).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 20:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ you not know, O addressees, ﴿that Allah has subjected to you what is in the heavens﴾ of the sun, the moon and the stars, so that you may benefit from them, ﴿and what is in the earth﴾ of fruits, rivers and animals, ﴿and has completed for you His favors outwardly and inwardly﴾ ﴿outwardly﴾ meaning beauty of form and proportion of limbs and other things, ﴿and inwardly﴾ meaning knowledge and other things. ﴿And among the people﴾ meaning the people of Makkah ﴿is one who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance﴾ from a messenger ﴿or a Book giving light﴾ sent down by Allah, ﴿but [follows] imitation (taqlid)﴾.
﴿And even if Satan were calling them to the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [meaning] its causes? No.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 22:

﴿And whoever submits his face to Allah﴾, i.e., turns toward His obedience, ﴿while he is a doer of good﴾, monotheist, ﴿has grasped the most trustworthy handhold﴾, by the strongest end, which will not fear its severing, ﴿and to Allah is the outcome of matters﴾, their return.

﴿And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you﴾, O Muhammad. Do not concern yourself with his disbelief. ﴿To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾, meaning of what is in them, as with others, and so He will recompense for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 24:

﴿We grant them enjoyment﴾ in the world ﴿for a little﴾ during the days of their lives; ﴿then We will compel them﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿to a harsh punishment﴾, which is the punishment of the Fire; they will find no escape from it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 25:

﴿And if﴾ the lam is a lam of oath (lam al-qasam). ﴿you ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they will surely say, "Allah."﴾ The nun of emphasis (nun al-raf') has been omitted from it because of the succession of similar letters (tawali al-amthal), and the waw of the pronoun because of the meeting of two quiescent letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn). ﴿Say: "Praise be to Allah."﴾ on the manifestation of the proof against them regarding the Oneness (tawhid). ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ its obligation upon them.

To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, in dominion, creation and servitude; so none other than Him deserves to be worshipped in them. Indeed God is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani), independent of His creation, the Praiseworthy (al-Hamid), praised in His handiwork.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 27:

﴿And if whatever trees are upon the earth were pens, and the sea [were ink], replenished thereafter by seven seas﴾ is a conjunction (ʿatf) upon the subject of inna (ism inna), ﴿as ink﴾ (midadan), ﴿the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ (mā nafidat kalimāt Allah), which are expressed thereby about His knowledge, by writing them with those pens and that ink, nor with anything more than that, because His knowledge, exalted is He, is not finite. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty﴾, nothing overpowers Him, ﴿Wise﴾, nothing falls outside His knowledge and wisdom.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 28:

﴿Your creation and your resurrection are not but as a single soul﴾, in creation and in resurrection, because He, by the word "Be," it is, ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing﴾, who hears every thing heard, ﴿All-Seeing﴾, who sees every thing seen, whom nothing distracts from anything.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 29:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ i.e., know, O addressee, ﴿that Allah causes the night to enter into the day﴾ i.e., makes it enter, ﴿and causes the day to enter into the night﴾ i.e., makes it enter into the night, so that each of them increases by what the other has lost. ﴿And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running﴾ in its orbit ﴿until a specified term﴾ which is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿That﴾ mentioned, ﴿because Allah is the Truth﴾ the established, ﴿and that what they invoke﴾ (read with the letter ي, ya', or the letter ت, ta') ﴿besides Him is falsehood﴾ the vanishing. ﴿And that Allah is the Most High﴾ over His creation through al-qahr (dominance by overpowering), ﴿the Great﴾ the Magnificent.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 31:

﴿Have you not seen that the ships﴾ (al-sufun) ﴿sail through the sea by the favor of Allah, that He may show you﴾ (O you being addressed by this) ﴿of His signs? Indeed in that are signs﴾ (ʿibar, lessons) ﴿for everyone who is steadfast﴾ (sabbar) ﴿in refraining from the disobedience of Allah, and grateful﴾ (shakur) ﴿for His favor.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 32:

﴿And when waves cover them like shades﴾ i.e., the disbelievers are overtaken; ﴿like shades﴾ like mountains that overshadow whatever is beneath them; ﴿they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ i.e., in supplication, that He may save them; i.e., they do not call upon anything along with Him. ﴿But when He delivers them to the land, some of them are moderate﴾ intermediate between disbelief and belief; ﴿and none reject Our signs except every treacherous ungrateful one﴾ treacherous, deceitful; ﴿ungrateful﴾ to the blessings of Allah, exalted is He.

O people, (i.e., the people of Makkah), fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail anything for his son, nor will a son avail anything for his father. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, in regard to the resurrection. So let not the worldly life deceive you (away from Islam), and let not the Deceiver (Satan) deceive you concerning Allah, through His forbearance and His respite.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 31, verse 34:

﴿Indeed, with Allah is the knowledge of the Hour﴾ when it will occur. ﴿And He sends down﴾ (with both the light and the intensive forms of the verb) ﴿the rain﴾ He sends down the rain at a time He knows. ﴿And He knows what is in the wombs﴾ whether it is male or female, and none knows any of these three except Allah the Exalted. ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾ of good or evil, and Allah the Exalted knows it. ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ and Allah the Exalted knows it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing﴾ of everything, ﴿Acquainted﴾ with its hidden aspects just as with its apparent ones. Al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn Umar a hadith: "The keys of the unseen are five: Indeed, with Allah is the knowledge of the Hour..." until the end of the surah.
